He highlighted the service calls and the different crimes experienced around the Region and the overall decrease in crime rates, with the exception of speeding. He noted the importance of utilization of the Community Safety and Well-Being Plan to actively invest in collaboration, youth, and advocacy. He clarified that there are eight (8) dedicated officers to address fraud incidents.

Council acknowledged the efforts of the WRPS during public events, specifically at the 2026 Victoria Day celebrations.

In response to Council, he explained that there are several initiatives to combat hate, such as the 'We All Belong Here' campaign, however, the trend toward radicalism and an increase to hate towards minority groups.

notes:
D. Bhatti introduced the presentation related to addressing the Council questions and resolutions from the Special Council meeting on June 3, 2026. A copy of the presentation was attached to the agenda.

Pam Law, Director, Projects (Water Capacity), provided an update on the Water Capacity Constraint, specifically the collaborative work that has been progressed to develop a framework that will allow for continued development. She provided a comparison on the impact of the water system when comparing the framework versus the proposed 10% resiliency. 

Council inquired into if proposed motion would fit in with the interim risk management framework (IRMF). Staff confirmed that allocation will be dealt with through the allocation policy and that it will work in conjunction with the IRMF. Staff also confirmed that the 20 l/s will be released as long as milestones are met and that no unforeseen circumstances arise that delay the construction of additional capacity. Staff also committed to continuing to provide Council with regular updates.

Council also inquired if currently approved subdivisions that wont be built for another one to three years are currently counted towards current demand on water. Staff elaborated that those subdivisions would not be counted towards current demand until approved through the applicable area municipalities' own allocation policy.

items.title: PDL-GDS-26-017, Proposed Approach to Servicing Agreement Transfer Requests within the Mannheim Service Area
notes:
Rod Regier, Commissioner, Planning, Development, and Legislative Services, provided an introduction to the report.

Council looked for confirmation on if water capacity is currently available for Activa's project. Amanda Kutler, Director, Regional Growth, Development, and Sustainability Services, explained that the capacity that was committed previously is not currently available as it was calculated using the previous methodology. This is why staff are looking to hold some capacity in reserve, so that it can meet the requirements of previously committed to projects. 

Staff also further clarified that it is not possible to move allocated water capacity around, as previous allocations no longer exist as the available capacity was calculated using the old methodology.

Staff further clarified that while some projects do still have valid water allocations, the Region can not support moving forward in development as no allocation actually exists as the previous allocation was calculated using a different methodology. 

Council inquired into how many liters per second are required for the Region to be able to fully support previously approved projects. Staff explained that they are currently operating using an average of 2.64 l/s for plans of subdivision on a quarterly basis. Using this average allows staff to adjust water allocation based on what developments come online in any given quarter.

motions.item_title: Administration and Finance Committee - June 2, 2026
motions.text: The Administration and Finance Committee recommends as follows: 1. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the revised Municipal Election Compliance Audit Committee Terms of Reference, as set out in Appendix A attached to report PDL-LEG-26-011, dated June 2, 2026. 2. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the 2026 first quarter update as set out in report COR-CFN-26-009 dated June 2, 2026: a) Receive the 2026 First Quarter Update that shows implementation and financial progress towards delivery on the Region’s Annual Business Plan, in support of achieving the vision set out by Council in the Growing with Care 2023-2027 Strategic Plan; and b) Amend the 2026 Capital Budget as set out in Appendix B. 3. Whereas Under the ESA, 2000, an employee is currently entitled to unpaid Reservist Leave for Canadian Forces training or deployment, provided they have at least two (2) months of continuous employment and Whereas if the employee is taking Reservist Leave because they are deployed to a Canadian Forces operation inside Canada related to handling an emergency or its aftermath, there is no minimum employment requirement and Whereas recent amendments via the Working for Workers Act, 2023, have expanded this leave to also include recovery from deployment-related injuries or illnesses and Whereas the current ESA leave type creates a "break in service" in OMERS, which can potentially reduce an employee’s credited service and future retirement benefits and Whereas, currently, the Region has not elected to share the cost of contributions, meaning that the employee is responsible for both their portion and the employer's portion, known as "double contributions" and Whereas OMERS regulations permit the purchase of service for certain leaves of absence, including those mandated by statute, to restore full credited service. For Reservist Leave, the employee may elect to buy back the period by contributing their share of premiums, with the employer matching its portion. This process requires explicit employer approval and, for municipal entities, formal authorization via a bylaw to ensure compliance with the Municipal Act, 2001, and to allocate public funds appropriately and Whereas the proposed bylaw will honour the employee's service to both the municipality and the nation, while upholding OMERS eligibility rules and Whereas the there are minimal financial implications associated with approving the OMERS Reservist Leave By-law and where an employee elects to take a Reservist Leave for Canadian Forces training or deployment, the Region as the employer will make an equal OMERS contribution in accordance with subsection 12(3) of the Primary Plan, funded from within the existing divisional operating budget, Now therefore be it resolved that the Region of Waterloo adopt the OMERS Region of Waterloo Reservist Bylaw to authorize the Region to match OMERS contributions for employees purchasing OMERS broken service resulting from an approved Reservist Leave, in accordance with the Employment Standards Act (ESA), 2000. 4. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve a By-law to delegate authority to the outgoing council to pass by-law(s) to authorize the potential adoption of the prudent investor standard, as set out in report COR-TRY-26-016 dated June 2, 2026. 5. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the 2027 Plan and Budget as set out in report COR-CFN-008 dated June 2, 2026: a) That staff be provided direction to present 2027 Plan and Budget timetable schedule to the incoming Regional Chair as set out in Appendix A.
motions.text_html:
The Administration and Finance Committee recommends as follows:


1.    That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the revised Municipal Election Compliance Audit Committee Terms of Reference, as set out in Appendix A attached to report PDL-LEG-26-011, dated June 2, 2026.


2.    That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the 2026 first quarter update as set out in report COR-CFN-26-009 dated June 2, 2026:


a)    Receive the 2026 First Quarter Update that shows implementation and financial progress towards delivery on the Region’s Annual Business Plan, in support of achieving the vision set out by Council in the Growing with Care 2023-2027 Strategic Plan; and 


b)    Amend the 2026 Capital Budget as set out in Appendix B.


3.    Whereas Under the ESA, 2000, an employee is currently entitled to unpaid Reservist Leave for Canadian Forces training or deployment, provided they have at least two (2) months of continuous employment and
Whereas if the employee is taking Reservist Leave because they are deployed to a Canadian Forces operation inside Canada related to handling an emergency or its aftermath, there is no minimum employment requirement and 
Whereas recent amendments via the Working for Workers Act, 2023, have expanded this leave to also include recovery from deployment-related injuries or illnesses and
Whereas the current ESA leave type creates a "break in service" in OMERS, which can potentially reduce an employee’s credited service and future retirement benefits and
Whereas, currently, the Region has not elected to share the cost of contributions, meaning that the employee is responsible for both their portion and the employer's portion, known as "double contributions" and 
Whereas OMERS regulations permit the purchase of service for certain leaves of absence, including those mandated by statute, to restore full credited service. For Reservist Leave, the employee may elect to buy back the period by contributing their share of premiums, with the employer matching its portion. This process requires explicit employer approval and, for municipal entities, formal authorization via a bylaw to ensure compliance with the Municipal Act, 2001, and to allocate public funds appropriately and 
Whereas the proposed bylaw will honour the employee's service to both the municipality and the nation, while upholding OMERS eligibility rules and 
Whereas the there are minimal financial implications associated with approving the OMERS Reservist Leave By-law and where an employee elects to take a Reservist Leave for Canadian Forces training or deployment, the Region as the employer will make an equal OMERS contribution in accordance with subsection 12(3) of the Primary Plan, funded from within the existing divisional operating budget, 
Now therefore be it resolved that the Region of Waterloo adopt the OMERS Region of Waterloo Reservist Bylaw to authorize the Region to match OMERS contributions for employees purchasing OMERS broken service resulting from an approved Reservist Leave, in accordance with the Employment Standards Act (ESA), 2000.


4.    That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve a By-law to delegate authority to the outgoing council to pass by-law(s) to authorize the potential adoption of the prudent investor standard, as set out in report COR-TRY-26-016 dated June 2, 2026.


5.    That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the 2027 Plan and Budget as set out in report COR-CFN-008 dated June 2, 2026:


a)    That staff be provided direction to present 2027 Plan and Budget timetable schedule to the incoming Regional Chair as set out in Appendix A.

motions.text: Whereas through ongoing work and updates to the Water Supply Strategy, Regional staff have identified a water capacity constraint within the Mannheim Service Area, which supplies water to Kitchener, Waterloo, and parts of Cambridge, Woolwich, and Wilmot. As a result, the Region of Waterloo has been unable to enter into any new servicing agreements or support the approval of development applications within this service area, until such time that sufficient capacity becomes available; Whereas the Region continues to work closely with its municipal partners on moving short term, medium term and long-term solutions forward as expeditiously as possible; Whereas Regional Council approved a Water Capacity Allocation Policy on May 6, 2026, for the Mannheim Service Area, which determines how available water will be allocated once it becomes available; Whereas Regional Council approved the Interim Risk Management Framework on June 3, 2026, which assesses how staged development could proceed under certain risk-based conditions in the Mannheim Service Area; Whereas the approved Interim Risk Management Framework outlined estimated water allocations to be provided to Area Municipalities by the Region on a quarterly basis, and where it is anticipated that growth would be supported by the end of September 2026; Whereas on June 3, 2026, Regional Council approved an additional allocation of 15 L/s from Wilmot Centre on an interim basis; Therefore, Be It Resolved that on July 1, 2026, 20L/s be assigned to Area Municipalities in alignment with the Council approved allocation policy and the IRMF, to be available for use no earlier than September 30, 2026; And further, be it resolved that future water allocations be assigned to Area Municipalities, by the Region, prior to, or on, the first day of the applicable quarter, beginning on October 1, 2026 for water to be available for use not sooner than the last day of the applicable quarter.
motions.text_html:
Whereas through ongoing work and updates to the Water Supply Strategy, Regional staff have identified a water capacity constraint within the Mannheim Service Area, which supplies water to Kitchener, Waterloo, and parts of Cambridge, Woolwich, and Wilmot. As a result, the Region of Waterloo has been unable to enter into any new servicing agreements or support the approval of development applications within this service area, until such time that sufficient capacity becomes available; 

Whereas the Region continues to work closely with its municipal partners on moving short term, medium term and long-term solutions forward as expeditiously as possible;

Whereas Regional Council approved a Water Capacity Allocation Policy on May 6, 2026, for the Mannheim Service Area, which determines how available water will be allocated once it becomes available;

Whereas Regional Council approved the Interim Risk Management Framework on June 3, 2026, which assesses how staged development could proceed under certain risk-based conditions in the Mannheim Service Area;

Whereas the approved Interim Risk Management Framework outlined estimated water allocations to be provided to Area Municipalities by the Region on a quarterly basis, and where it is anticipated that growth would be supported by the end of September 2026; 

Whereas on June 3, 2026, Regional Council approved an additional allocation of 15 L/s from Wilmot Centre on an interim basis;  

Therefore, Be It Resolved that on July 1, 2026, 20L/s be assigned to Area Municipalities in alignment with the Council approved allocation policy and the IRMF, to be available for use no earlier than September 30, 2026; 

 And further, be it resolved that future water allocations be assigned to Area Municipalities, by the Region, prior to, or on, the first day of the applicable quarter, beginning on October 1, 2026 for water to be available for use not sooner than the last day of the applicable quarter.

motions.item_title: PDL-GDS-26-018, Forward Looking Service Agreements (Response to Resolution 4)
motions.text: Whereas through ongoing work and updates to the Water Supply Strategy, Region of Waterloo staff have identified a water capacity constraint within the Mannheim Service Area, which supplies water to Kitchener, Waterloo, and parts of Cambridge, Woolwich, and Wilmot. As a result, the Region has currently been unable to enter into any new servicing agreements or support the approval of development applications within this service area, until such time that sufficient capacity becomes available; Whereas the Region continues to work closely with its municipal partners on moving short, medium, and long-term solutions forward as expeditiously as possible; Whereas Regional Council approved a Water Capacity Allocation Policy on May 6, 2026, for the Mannheim Service Area, which determines how available water will be allocated once it becomes available: Whereas Regional Council approved the Interim Risk Management Framework on June 3, 2026, which assesses how staged development can proceed under certain risk-based conditions in the Mannheim Service Area; Whereas the details of any Municipal Forward Facing/Looking Servicing Agreements (MFSA’s) rest solely with Area Municipalities with respect to Planning Act and Building Code Act approvals; Whereas there are existing draft plans of subdivision that received draft approval prior to May 6, 2026, and which require a servicing agreement as a condition of draft plan approval, may be exempt from this motion; Therefore, be it resolved that the Region of Waterloo prepare an administrative agreement in conjunction with Area Municipalities by July 8, 2026 for execution by all relevant parties to implement the Regional Water Allocation Framework which will enable water allocation by the Region to an area municipalities in accordance with the Interim Risk Management Framework (IRMF) allocation schedule, as presented on June 3, 2026, with the following: Estimated Overall Allocation July 1, 2026 - 20 L/S October 1, 2026 - 40 L/S January 1, 2027 - 55 L/S July 1, 2028 - 25 L/S October 1, 2028 - 50 L/S July 1, 2030 - 45 L/S October 1, 2030 - 60 L/S and January 1, 2031 - 20 L/S; and, Further, Be It Resolved that such Administrative Agreements aim to include the following provisions, namely: Requirement for area municipalities to report all building permits to the Region for ongoing monitoring of water allocated against their share of the above allocation table, Notification processes for the Region to inform area municipalities if available water capacity is more than projected in the above table, or available earlier than expected, Notification timing provisions for the Region to notify Area Municipalities if it cannot meet the IRMF allocation schedule as listed above, Force Majeure clause, in case the Region is unable to meet its anticipated additional allocations due to an act outside of its control; and Further, Be It Resolved that the Region of Waterloo enable any area municipality to enter into Forward Facing/Looking Servicing Agreements for developments subject to the allocation table above; and Further, Be It Resolved that the Region coordinate any required regional approvals, required by an Area Municipality’s Forward Facing Servicing Agreements (MFSA), such approvals not to be withheld as long as the MFSA’s were issued within the parameters of the above allocation tables and the requirements of such approvals are met; And Finally, Be It Resolved that except in the case of draft plans of subdivision that were draft approved prior to May 6, and which may be exempt from this motion, all Forward Facing/Looking Servicing Agreements shall be executed between an Area Municipality and the property owner, in accordance with the overall water allocation granted to an Area Municipality by the Region.
motions.text_html:
Whereas through ongoing work and updates to the Water Supply Strategy, Region of Waterloo staff have identified a water capacity constraint within the Mannheim Service Area, which supplies water to Kitchener, Waterloo, and parts of Cambridge, Woolwich, and Wilmot. As a result, the Region has currently been unable to enter into any new servicing agreements or support the approval of development applications within this service area, until such time that sufficient capacity becomes available; 

Whereas the Region continues to work closely with its municipal partners on moving short, medium, and long-term solutions forward as expeditiously as possible;

Whereas Regional Council approved a Water Capacity Allocation Policy on May 6, 2026, for the Mannheim Service Area, which determines how available water will be allocated once it becomes available:

Whereas Regional Council approved the Interim Risk Management Framework on June 3, 2026, which assesses how staged development can proceed under certain risk-based conditions in the Mannheim Service Area;

Whereas the details of any Municipal Forward Facing/Looking Servicing Agreements (MFSA’s) rest solely with Area Municipalities with respect to Planning Act and Building Code Act approvals;

Whereas there are existing draft plans of subdivision that received draft approval prior to May 6, 2026, and which require a servicing agreement as a condition of draft plan approval, may be exempt from this motion; 

Therefore, be it resolved that the Region of Waterloo prepare an administrative agreement in conjunction with Area Municipalities by July 8, 2026 for execution by all relevant parties to implement the Regional Water Allocation Framework which will enable water allocation by the Region to an area municipalities  in accordance with the Interim Risk Management Framework (IRMF) allocation schedule, as presented on June 3, 2026, with the following: 

Estimated Overall Allocation

  •  July 1, 2026 - 20 L/S
  • October 1, 2026 - 40 L/S
  • January 1, 2027 - 55 L/S
  • July 1, 2028 - 25 L/S
  • October 1, 2028 - 50 L/S
  • July 1, 2030 - 45 L/S
  • October 1, 2030 - 60 L/S and
  • January 1, 2031 - 20 L/S; and,

Further, Be It Resolved that such Administrative Agreements aim to include the following provisions, namely:

  • Requirement for area municipalities to report all building permits to the Region for ongoing monitoring of water allocated against their share of the above allocation table,
  • Notification processes for the Region to inform area municipalities if available water capacity is more than projected in the above table, or available earlier than expected,
  • Notification timing provisions for the Region to notify Area Municipalities if it cannot meet the IRMF allocation schedule as listed above,
  • Force Majeure clause, in case the Region is unable to meet its anticipated additional allocations due to an act outside of its control; and

Further, Be It Resolved that the Region of Waterloo enable any area municipality to enter into Forward Facing/Looking Servicing Agreements for developments subject to the allocation table above; and

Further, Be It Resolved that the Region coordinate any required regional approvals, required by an Area Municipality’s Forward Facing Servicing Agreements (MFSA), such approvals not to be withheld as long as the MFSA’s were issued within the parameters of the above allocation tables and the requirements of such approvals are met;  

And Finally, Be It Resolved that except in the case of draft plans of subdivision that were draft approved prior to May 6, and which may be exempt from this motion, all Forward Facing/Looking Servicing Agreements shall be executed between an Area Municipality and the property owner, in accordance with the overall water allocation granted to an Area Municipality by the Region.

motions.item_title: Councillor M. Rodrigues
motions.text: WHEREAS there is a need to support and manage the continued operations of The Hydrocut trail system and its role as a major destination in Ontario and beyond, since the original Stewardship Agreement was signed in 2009; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT the Commissioner of Planning, Development, and Legislative Services: 1. Report to Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee in Fall 2026 on potential amendments to the existing Stewardship Agreement with The Hydrocut operations on Regional property, including continued mountain bike trail development identified therein; and 2. Engage with The Hydrocut through the ongoing Regional Forest Management Plan to identify a long-term strategy for access, servicing, land, and forest management.

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT the Commissioner of Planning, Development, and Legislative Services:

2.    Engage with The Hydrocut through the ongoing Regional Forest Management Plan to identify a long-term strategy for access, servicing, land, and forest management.
